**[0:00] B1 · The 2026 landfill ban**
- slow down, serious tone
"So far I've mostly shown you things that worked. This one started in January, and it's not going well."

**[0:25] B2 · The ban**
- passed 2021, five years to prepare · little new burning capacity added · started on time
- Gyeonggi (gyung-gee) · burying raw trash banned · now burned or processed first

**[0:55] B3 · After the ban**
- public burning up only 80 t · private handling up 3.2× · only 4 incinerators

**[1:30] B4 · Where the trash goes**
- Gangdong (gahng-dong) to Cheonan (chuh-nahn), Sejong (seh-jong)
- Gangnam plans Cheongju (chung-joo) · map is straight-line, news says 130 km by road

**[2:05] B5 · Pushback**
- Cheongju companies: no Seoul-area bids through the end of next year
- trash sent to cities that didn't make it (environmental justice)
- Seongnam (sung-nahm) building a 500 t/day incinerator

**[2:30] B6 · The question for New York**
- LL97 fines buildings over their caps · about 63% projected to miss 2030 caps if nothing changes
- ask, then stop and wait
"Seoul banned burying trash before it had enough incinerators. Can New York's retrofit workers and supply chain keep up with LL97?"
